newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Regulator wants TNT freeze extended.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Regulator wants TNT freeze extended.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission said on Tuesday it will seek to extend a freeze order on about A$10 million of trading profits in TNT Ltd options when the case is again heard in the Federal Court on Thursday.
"We will be asking for a continuation and the investigation will continue," a spokeswoman for the corporate regulator said.
She said the case revolved around the dealings of one individual and two companies.
The individual provided the apparently fictitious name of Mark Booth, she said, and had a postal address in suburban Sydney which had no follow-on contact.

The Australian Financial Review newspaper said on Tuesday that "Booth" had made a profit of A$2.0 million from trading in TNT options just before a takeover bid for TNT was announced by Dutch postal and telecoms group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV last Wednesday.
The options dealt in by Booth had a conversion price of A$2.00 which was "out of the money" until KPN offered A$2.45 per share in cash fo TNT, the paper said.
